name: Grand Prix 5000 S TR

origin.basis: Continental's bicycle tires are marketed from its German site; Germany-made lines are marked 'Handmade in Germany'.

positioning: Continental's tubeless race and all-round road tire, positioned as a balance of speed, grip and puncture protection.
hookless_note: Continental lists separate hookless maximum pressures (73 psi up to 28 mm, 65 psi at 30-32 mm, 58 psi at 35 mm) and permitted rim ranges per size.
weight_basis: Continental black-sidewall claims per size; transparent sidewalls add up to 5 g.
pressure_note: Maximum pressures are for hooked rims; hookless limits are lower.

availability.note: Continental's official Tmall store sells it in mainland China; Continental's German and US catalogs list it for retailers.

caveats: Use the lower hookless pressure on hookless rims and stay inside the permitted rim range for the size.
Fast, light race casing: tread puncture protection measured lower than all-season and training tires.
Check frame and rim clearance for the measured width; tires usually measure wider on wide rims.

owner_evidence.screening_note: Coded on 2026-11-03 from a fixed source set: every reader comment on Bicycle Rolling Resistance's test pages for this tire, the written customer reviews that bike-components and Sigma Sports serve on their product pages (reviews loaded by third-party widgets were not read) and owner comments in the coded Xiaohongshu threads. Counted only owners who describe their own riding; star-only ratings, mounting-only impressions and repeats were left out. Reviews of the transparent-sidewall edition and comments about the earlier GP5000 TL were not counted.

reports.summary: Bought as a successor to the GP5000 TL: a really fast tire, but without that tire's puncture resistance.
Light, easy to seat tubeless and confidence-inspiring even in the rain; no puncture apart from a drain-grate accident that cut a front sidewall, and the owner found the sidewalls soft at 80 psi.
Really good tires, though the owner prefers a Vittoria Corsa Speed and keeps these for winter riding.
As fast as the owner's 30 mm tires, very comfortable on rough roads and exceptional grip wet or dry; no puncture so far, though sealant may have closed small holes.
Hard to mount and seat; when the sealant was refreshed after five months it had closed eight punctures, against one or two in the owner's previous Schwalbe tires.
Rode them for 8,000 km without problems and liked the road feel.
Felt slightly vague in fast corners compared with the ARISUN tubeless tire that replaced it.
